clue.text: British political schemer's ultimately unfair to wrongly rate MP

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: done wrongly, the letters of rate and MP are put in the wrong order
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of unfair is used

explanation.surface: A complaint that an MP has been unfairly marked down by a scheming British politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' turns RATEMP into MRTAPE, and the R from the end of 'unfair' finishes the name. Mr Taper is a party wire-puller in Disraeli's political novel Coningsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Taper is Disraeli's caricature of a scheming party manager in the novel Coningsby, so he is a fictional British political intriguer.

clue.text: Boss who isn't in Chekhovian drama, with staff and no-good crew

definitions.text: Boss who isn't in Chekhovian drama

parts.note: to staff a ship or office is to man it

indicators.note: G is short for good, so no-good means the letter G is dropped

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers or villains

explanation.surface: A drama of a boss with his staff and a worthless crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw subtitled Heartbreak House 'A Fantasia in the Russian Manner', so it is the Chekhovian drama; its 'Boss' Mangan turns out not to be rich at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shaw's Heartbreak House the industrialist called Boss Mangan proves to be a sham tycoon, a boss in name only.

clue.text: 3 is a book by Gertrude Stein

parts.note: the figure 3 written as a word
to be or exist is to live, so 'is' becomes 'lives'

explanation.surface: A statement that the number 3 is the title of a Stein book.
explanation.definitionFit: Stein's 1909 collection of three novellas about working women bears this title.

clue.text: Work on action to support a leaderless country

indicators.note: in a down clue, one part placed on another comes above it in the grid

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: without its leader, the country loses its first letter

parts.note: Uganda is an African country
a play is a move or action, as in a sporting play

explanation.surface: A call for work to be done on taking action to help a country without a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the U of UGANDA to leave GANDA; 'on' sets PROP A GANDA above PLAY in this down entry, and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama written to push a political message is a piece of theatre, a dramatic work.

clue.text: Bishop quits bankrupt, according to a Walter Scott poem

indicators.note: the bishop quits, meaning that letter leaves the word

parts.note: someone bankrupt is broke
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
by means according to, as in 'by the rules'

explanation.surface: A bishop leaving a bankrupt diocese, as told in Scott's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' takes B out of BROKE to leave ROKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rokeby is Scott's 1813 narrative poem set in Teesdale during the English Civil War.

clue.text: Little Beatrice, wellahead but thrashed

parts.note: Bea is a short form of the name Beatrice
well ahead in a game, say ten points up

explanation.surface: A girl called Beatrice was winning comfortably but then lost heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten up is to be thrashed or assaulted, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Where to learn performance skills shared by opera and dance

indicators.note: shared by says the answer is split, with a part sitting at the tail of the word opera
and carries the sharing on to the next word, whose opening holds the other part

explanation.surface: A question about where performing skills common to opera and ballet can be taught.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles two words with 'and' ignored between them. RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Academy of Dramatic Art is a leading London drama school where actors train.

clue.text: Office, late at night, servingbeer — neat

indicators.note: beer served is beer prepared and dished up, a sign its letters are reworked along with neat

explanation.surface: A night-time scene at work with beer poured neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' rearranges BEER and NEAT. Office here is a church service; 'Office' wants to mean a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenebrae is the Holy Week service of matins and lauds, traditionally sung in darkness, one of the canonical Offices.

clue.text: Part of a sporting championship that can be seen at the Crucible Theatre

definitions.meaning: a stage of a golf or tennis Open tournament

definitions.text: can be seen at the Crucible Theatre
definitions.meaning: the Sheffield theatre has a thrust stage open on three sides

explanation.surface: The Crucible in Sheffield, home of the world snooker championship, staging part of a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible Theatre in Sheffield hosts the World Snooker Championship, which tempts a sporting reading of the second half too.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage with the audience on several sides is called an open or thrust stage, as at Sheffield's theatre.

clue.text: Undesirables in an ArthurKoestler book

definitions.meaning: the lowest, most despised people in society
Koestler's 1941 memoir of internment in France

explanation.surface: Unwanted people appearing in a book by Arthur Koestler.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the most worthless of people, and Koestler used it as the title of his memoir about French camps.

clue.text: Type of terrier seen in three Shakespeare plays

definitions.meaning: a small, wiry breed of dog from East Anglia
the Duke of this title appears in Henry VI Part 3, Richard III and Henry VIII

explanation.surface: A dog breed that turns up in three of Shakespeare's histories.
explanation.walkthrough: NORFOLK is an English county, which gives both a terrier breed and a ducal title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk terrier is a small breed with folded ears, and the Duke of that county is a Shakespearean character.

clue.text: Companions of Tolkien character, before the present day

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: Ents are the tree-like creatures in The Lord of the Rings
the present day is our age

explanation.surface: Companions of a figure from Tolkien who lived long before our own time.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue of attendants and companions surrounding an important person is a synonym here.

clue.text: Famous actress seen in a 1939 Shaw play

definitions.meaning: a celebrated Restoration stage performer, mistress of Charles II
she is a character in Shaw's In Good King Charles's Golden Days

explanation.surface: A star actress appearing in one of Shaw's late plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Restoration actress who became Charles II's mistress appears as a character in Shaw's 1939 comedy about the king.

clue.text: Mischief-maker consumed by gold in a tale about frontiersmen

indicators.note: one thing consumed by another is swallowed up inside it

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A troublemaker swallowed up by greed for gold in a story of pioneers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is a Greek goddess, not the verb; 'consumed by' is the container signal, not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A Western film or story, about cowboys and frontier life, is informally called this, from the horses' oats.

clue.text: Some nuns in a Gore Vidal novel

definitions.meaning: a pair of nuns, each one called sister
Vidal's 1970 novel about a brother and sister

explanation.surface: A few nuns appearing in a book by Gore Vidal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of nuns is a couple of religious sisters, and Vidal's 1970 book bears that title.

clue.text: He wrote poetry about an angel and witches, disturbing Mary Potter

definitions.text: He wrote poetry about an angel

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

indicators.note: disturbing the name Mary Potter muddles its letters

explanation.surface: A poet whose work on an angel and witches upsets someone called Mary Potter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges MARYPOTTER into TRYPATMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian poet's best-known sequence is The Angel in the House, a verse portrait of the ideal wife.

clue.text: Numbers about a musical movie's handsome prince, on screen initially

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
Hans is the handsome prince in Disney's musical film Frozen
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word screen

explanation.surface: Songs about a handsome film prince shown on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers are songs, and French songs in a cabaret style are called by this French word.

clue.text: Someonelike 22's story-telling

definitions.meaning: someone like an aunt is a family member; the 's stands for 'is'
the act of narrating or recounting events

explanation.surface: Someone resembling a relative from 22 is a born storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is AUNT, a kinswoman; a second sense of the word is a narration, as in 'the relation of events'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman or kinswoman is a relative, and recounting a story is a narration, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Here RichardParker was confused

definitions.meaning: the tiger Richard Parker spends Life of Pi adrift in a lifeboat on the ocean

explanation.surface: A man named Richard Parker was bewildered here.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Parker reads like a person, but he is the Bengal tiger in Yann Martel's Life of Pi.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adrift on the ocean and being bewildered share one idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Latin poet's cryptic clue about right case for reflection

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: one piece going about another wraps around it
a cryptic version of the word clue is a puzzling rearrangement of its letters
a reflection shows the word backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: a suit is a case at law

explanation.surface: A Latin poet is mentioned in a crossword clue about a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges the word clue, 'about' wraps that round right, and 'for reflection' turns the case backwards; the definition's 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucretius was the Roman author of De Rerum Natura, a philosophical poem in Latin hexameters.

clue.text: Posh boy to tick off about Latin

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: to tick off someone is to chide them

explanation.surface: A public-school boy being reprimanded about his Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside CHIDE. A childe is an archaic word for a youth of noble birth, as in Byron's Childe Harold.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic title was given to a young man of noble birth awaiting knighthood, a highborn youth.

clue.text: Assist somehow when nothing is happening

indicators.note: done somehow, by some unspecified means, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying to help in some way at a time when things are idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ASSIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of inactivity or equilibrium where nothing changes is what the word describes.

clue.text: It's time to work with Clara for this composer

indicators.note: to work the letters is to rework them into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician says it is time to start working with Clara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges ITS, T and CLARA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian Baroque keyboard composer famous for his harpsichord sonatas.

clue.text: ForGreene'straveller, it's hard to leave a favourite place

definitions.note: Graham Greene's novel Travels with My Aunt follows a globetrotting elderly relative

indicators.note: the letter leaves, dropping out of the word

parts.note: a haunt is a place one visits often
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A traveller in a Greene novel finds it hard to leave a beloved spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes H out of HAUNT. 'For' is part of the definition phrase, since the traveller in Greene's book is the narrator's relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Greene's Travels with My Aunt centres on the narrator's adventurous elderly kinswoman Augusta.

clue.text: Generosity that's shown by Scrooge (small)

parts.note: the name Scrooge begins with a capital, that is a large S

explanation.surface: An ironic remark that the miser Scrooge shows only a little generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface mocks the miser in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, but 'Scrooge' is read as written: it opens with a large S, and 'small' adds a little s.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is lavish giving or bounty, generosity bestowed freely on others.

clue.text: French peer who lived in Camberwell in a George Gissing novel

definitions.text: who lived in Camberwell in a George Gissing novel

parts.note: Nancy is a French city in Lorraine
a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat who lived in a South London district in a Gissing novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Camberwell is a district of South London. The heroine of Gissing's In the Year of Jubilee lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Lord is the heroine of Gissing's 1894 novel In the Year of Jubilee, set among the Camberwell middle class.

clue.text: Apparent recipient of a famous letter — he's found in English work after introduction

definitions.text: Apparent recipient of a famous letter

indicators.note: one thing found in another sits inside it
after its introduction means once the first letter is gone

parts.note: an opus is a work
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man found writing in English is named as the addressee of a famous epistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after introduction' removes the first letter of the work, and 'found in' sets he's inside what is left. The letter is St Paul's epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Epistle to the Ephesians was addressed to the church of that Greek city, though scholars doubt its destination.
